segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Twelve. Construct a perpendicular to a given line from a given point not on it. Given line A B and point C not on it, we are to construct from C a segment perpendicular to line A B.

subsegments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Twelve. Construct a perpendicular to a given line from a given point not on it. Given line A B and point C not on it, we are to construct from C a segment perpendicular to line A B.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: First, take a point D on the other side of line A B, and by Postulate Three, construct circle C D, with center C and defining radius point D. Circle C D intersects line A B at two points, E and G. Next, by Proposition Ten, bisect segment E G at point H, so that G H equals H E. Finally, by Postulate One, construct segments C G, C H, and C E.

subsegments.text: First, take a point D on the other side of line A B, and by Postulate Three, construct circle C D, with center C and defining radius point D. segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Since point C is the center of circle C D, Definition Fifteen guarantees that radius C G equals radius C E. Now compare triangles C H G and C H E: side G H equals side E H, side H C is common to both, and base C G equals base C E—so by Proposition Eight, Side-Side-Side congruence, the adjacent angles C H G and E H C are equal. And by Definition Ten, when a segment standing on a line makes the adjacent angles equal, each angle is a right angle and the standing segment is perpendicular to the line. Therefore segment C H has been constructed perpendicular to line A B from point C not on it, as was required to do.
